24:12.headline: They did not know whether he deserved to die at all
24:12.body: Rashi compares this to the man who gathered wood on the Sabbath. There they knew he must die but not how, while here the word לפרש shows they did not know if he deserved death at all.

sources.quote: וְיוֹדְעִים הָיוּ שֶׁהַמְּקוֹשֵׁשׁ בְּמִיתָה, אֲבָל לֹא פֹרַשׁ לָהֶם בְּאֵיזוֹ מִיתָה
sources.says: Rashi says they knew the wood gatherer would be put to death, but not by which death.

sources.quote: אֲבָל בַּמְּקַלֵּל הוּא אוֹמֵר לִפְרֹשׁ לָהֶם, שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ יוֹדְעִים אִם חַיָּב מִיתָה אִם לָאו
sources.says: Rashi says for the blasphemer it says 'to explain to them' because they did not know whether he was liable to death.

24:20.headline: 'Eye for an eye' is paid in money, hence 'given'
24:20.body: The sages read 'so shall it be given to him' as payment, not a matching injury. Rashi says that is why the verse uses the word for giving: money passes from hand to hand.

sources.quote: שֶׁאֵינוֹ נְתִינַת מוּם מַמָּשׁ אֶלָּא תַּשְׁלוּמֵי מָמוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says it is not the actual giving of an injury but payment of money.

sources.quote: לְכָךְ כָּתוּב בּוֹ לְשׁוֹן נְתִינָה — דָּבָר הַנָּתוּן מִיָּד לְיָד
sources.says: Rashi says that is why it is written with the word for giving: something handed from one hand to another.

sources.quote: כי לא יתכן להיות שבר תחת שבר כמשמעו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra cites the Gaon: 'a break for a break' cannot be meant literally.

24:22.headline: The stranger is a seed carried off, the citizen a rooted tree
24:22.body: Rabbeinu Bahya explains both words with a picture. A גר is like a grain that has come loose from its tree, and an אזרח is like a tree planted long ago, as in 'a well-rooted native tree'.

sources.quote: ונפרד מארצו נקרא גר, מלשון גרגיר הנפרד מן האילן
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says one who has left his land is called גר, from the word for a berry that has separated from the tree.

sources.quote: ומי שאבותיו מן העיר נקרא אזרח, מלשון (תהילים ל״ז:ל״ה) ומתערה כאזרח רענן, כדמיון הנטיעה הנטועה מימי קדם
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says one whose fathers are from the city is called אזרח, like a sapling planted long ago.

25:1.headline: What does the sabbatical year have to do with Sinai?
25:1.body: All the commandments came from Sinai, so why name Sinai here? The Sifra answers that it is an example: just as every detail of the sabbatical year was given at Sinai, so were the details of all the other laws.

sources.quote: מה ענין שמיטה אצל הר סיני? והלא כל המצות נאמרו מסיני
sources.says: The Sifra asks what the sabbatical year has to do with Mount Sinai, since all the commandments were said at Sinai.

sources.quote: אֶלָּא מַה שְּׁמִטָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ כְלָלוֹתֶיהָ וּפְרָטוֹתֶיהָ וְדִקְדּוּקֶיהָ מִסִּינַי אַף כֻּלָּן נֶאֶמְרוּ כְלָלוֹתֵיהֶן וְדִקְדּוּקֵיהֶן מִסִּינַי
sources.says: Rashi says that just as the sabbatical year's general rules and fine details were said at Sinai, so were those of all the commandments.

25:5.headline: Grapes you kept apart, like a nazir keeps apart
25:5.body: נזיר usually means a person set apart by a vow. Here Rashi says it means the vines you fenced off and kept from other people. In the seventh year you may not harvest them as your own.

sources.quote: שֶׁהִנְזַרְתָּ וְהִפְרַשְׁתָּ בְנֵי אָדָם מֵהֶם וְלֹא הִפְקַרְתָּם
sources.says: Rashi says these are the grapes you kept people away from and did not leave open to all.

sources.quote: נזירך ידוע שהוא מגזרת נזיר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says נזירך clearly comes from the same root as נזיר.

25:10.headline: Freedom, like a bird that lives wherever it likes
25:10.body: Rabbi Yehudah says דרור means a person who lives wherever he wants and trades in every land. Ibn Ezra adds that the דרור is also a small bird that sings when free, but in a cage will not eat until it dies.

sources.quote: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: מָה לְשׁוֹן דְּרוֹר — כִּמְדַיַּיר בֵּי דַיָּירָא, וּמוֹבִיל סְחוֹרָה בְּכׇל מְדִינָה
sources.says: Rabbi Yehudah says דרור is like one who lives in any dwelling and carries goods to every country.

sources.quote: שֶׁדָּר בְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁהוּא רוֹצֶה וְאֵינוֹ בִרְשׁוּת אֲחֵרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means one who lives wherever he wants and is not under the control of others.

sources.quote: וכדרור לעוף עוף קטן מנגן כשהוא ברשותו ואם הוא ברשות אדם לא יאכל עד שימות
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the דרור is a small bird that sings when it is free, and in a person's keeping will not eat until it dies.

25:10.headline: The jubilee: named for the ram's horn, or for coming home
25:10.body: Rashi says יובל is named for the shofar blast. Ibn Ezra reads it as sending free. Ramban rejects the shofar reading and says it means being brought: in this year each person is brought back to his land and family.

sources.quote: יוֹבֵל שְׁמָהּ, עַל שֵׁם תְּקִיעַת שׁוֹפָר
sources.says: Rashi says its name is יובל because of the shofar blowing.

sources.quote: יובל. כמו שלוח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says יובל means sending free.

sources.quote: וּלְפִי דַּעְתִּי לֹא קְרָאוֹ הַכָּתוּב יוֹבֵל עַל הַתְּקִיעָה, רַק עַל הַדְּרוֹר
sources.says: Ramban says that in his view the verse did not name it for the shofar blast but for the freedom.

sources.quote: שֶׁבָּהּ יוּבַל כָּל אִישׁ אֶל אֲחֻזָּתוֹ וְאֶל מִשְׁפַּחְתּוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says in this year each man is brought back to his land and his family.

25:17.headline: The same word twice: cheating with money, then hurting with words
25:17.body: The verb ונה, to wrong, appears in verse 14 and again here. Rashi says verse 14 is about cheating in a sale. This verse is about wronging with words: taunting someone, or giving bad advice for your own gain.

sources.quote: אל תונו. זוֹ אוֹנָאַת מָמוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the first one, in verse 14, means cheating with money.

sources.quote: כָּאן הִזְהִיר עַל אוֹנָאַת דְּבָרִים, שֶׁלֹּא יַקְנִיט אֶת חֲבֵרוֹ וְלֹא יַשִּׂיאֶנּוּ עֵצָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ הוֹגֶנֶת לוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says here the warning is about wronging with words: not to taunt your fellow or give him advice that is not good for him.

25:35.headline: Hold him up before he falls
25:35.body: Rashi reads והחזקת as catching someone as he starts to slip, before he hits bottom. A load slipping off a donkey can be held by one person. Once it falls to the ground, five people cannot lift it.

sources.quote: אַל תַּנִּיחֵהוּ שֶׁיֵּרֵד וְיִפֹּל וְיִהְיֶה קָשֶׁה לַהֲקִימוֹ, אֶלָּא חַזְּקֵהוּ מִשְּׁעַת מוֹטַת הַיָּד
sources.says: Rashi says do not let him go down and fall, when it is hard to raise him, but strengthen him from the moment his hand starts to slip.

sources.quote: לְמַשּׂאוֹי שֶׁעַל הַחֲמוֹר, עוֹדֵהוּ עַל הַחֲמוֹר אֶחָד תּוֹפֵס בּוֹ וּמַעֲמִידוֹ, נָפַל לָאָרֶץ, חֲמִשָּׁה אֵין מַעֲמִידִין אוֹתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi compares it to a load on a donkey: while it is still on, one person can hold it, but once it falls, five cannot lift it.

25:36.headline: Interest is called a bite
25:36.body: נשך means a bite, as a snake bites. The Mishnah says this kind of interest is called נשך because it bites: the lender takes from the borrower something he never gave.

sources.quote: הַמַּלְוֶה סֶלַע בַּחֲמִשָּׁה דִּינָרִין, סָאתַיִם חִטִּין בְּשָׁלֹשׁ – אָסוּר, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא נוֹשֵׁךְ
sources.says: The Mishnah says lending a coin for five dinars back, or two measures of wheat for three, is forbidden because it bites.

sources.quote: נֶשֶׁךְ אִיכָּא – דְּקָא נָכֵית לֵיהּ, דְּקָא שָׁקֵיל מִינֵּיהּ מִידֵּי דְּלָא יָהֵיב
sources.says: The Talmud says it is biting because he takes from him something he did not give.

25:41.headline: Back to his fathers' land, and back to his fathers' honor
25:41.body: אחזה usually means a land holding. Rashi says here it means the standing and honor of his fathers. A man freed from servitude must not be looked down on because he was once sold.

sources.quote: אֶל כְּבוֹד אֲבוֹתָיו, וְאֵין לְזַלְזְלוֹ בְּכָךְ
sources.says: Rashi says it means to the honor of his fathers, and he must not be belittled for this.

25:43.headline: Harsh work means work with no purpose
25:43.body: Rashi says פרך is work given only to wear a person down, like telling him to warm a cup you do not need. Since only the master knows if the job is needed, the verse adds: fear your God. On the same word in Egypt, one sage reads בפרך as בפה רך, with a soft mouth.

sources.quote: מְלָאכָה שֶׁלֹּא לְצֹרֶךְ, כְּדֵי לְעַנּוֹתוֹ, אַל תֹּאמַר לוֹ, הָחֵם לִי אֶת הַכּוֹס הַזֶּה וְהוּא אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ
sources.says: Rashi says it means needless work meant to afflict him, such as telling him to heat a cup that is not needed.

sources.quote: לָא תִפְלַח בֵּיהּ בְּקַשְׁיוּ
sources.says: Onkelos translates: do not work him harshly.

sources.quote: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר: בְּפֶה רַךְ. רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: בִּפְרִיכָה
sources.says: On the same word in the Egyptian slavery, Rabbi Elazar reads it as with a soft mouth and Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani as crushing work.

25:55.headline: My servants, and not servants of servants
25:55.body: Rashi says God's claim came first, like an earlier deed. The Talmud says this is why a servant who chooses to stay is pierced at the ear: that ear heard at Sinai that Israel are God's servants, not servants to servants.

sources.quote: כי לי בני ישראל עבדים. שְׁטָרִי קוֹדֵם
sources.says: Rashi says Israel are My servants because My deed came first.

sources.quote: אֹזֶן שֶׁשָּׁמְעָה קוֹלִי עַל הַר סִינַי בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי: ״כִּי לִי בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲבָדִים״ – וְלֹא עֲבָדִים לַעֲבָדִים, וְהָלַךְ זֶה וְקָנָה אָדוֹן לְעַצְמוֹ – יֵרָצַע
sources.says: Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai says the ear that heard at Sinai that Israel are God's servants, not servants of servants, and then went and took a master for itself, should be pierced.

26:1.headline: A stone floor to bow on, or a carved stone
26:1.body: Rashi reads משכית from covering: a floor paved with stones, where people stretched out flat to bow. Ibn Ezra reads it as a stone with pictures on it, from משכיות, things that catch the eye.

sources.quote: לְשׁוֹן כִּסּוּי, כְּמוֹ "וְשַׂכֹּתִי כַפִּי" (שמות ל"ג), שֶׁמְּכַסִּין הַקַּרְקַע בְּרִצְפַּת אֲבָנִים
sources.says: Rashi says it means covering, because they cover the ground with a stone floor.

sources.quote: וטעמו אבן מצויירת מגזרת עברו משכיות לבב שכיות החמד
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means a stone with images, from the word for fancies of the heart and lovely sights.

26:3.headline: Walking in My laws means toiling in Torah study
26:3.body: The verse already says to keep and do the commandments. So the Sifra and Rashi ask what walking in My laws adds. Their answer: to labor hard at learning Torah.

sources.quote: הָא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּם אִם בְּחֻקֹּתַי תֵּלֵכוּ? שֶׁתִּהְיוּ עֲמֵלִים בַּתּוֹרָה
sources.says: Rashi says walking in My laws means that you should toil in Torah.

sources.quote: הא מה אני מקיים "אם בחקתי תלכו"? להיות עמלים בתורה
sources.says: The Sifra says the phrase means to be toiling in Torah, since keeping the commandments is said separately.

26:21.headline: Walking with God by chance, or in stubborn defiance
26:21.body: קרי is used only in this chapter. The sages read it as by chance: keeping the commandments now and then. Rashi also gives Menachem's reading, holding back, and Onkelos's, stubbornness. Ibn Ezra reports a view that it means defiant toughness.

sources.quote: רַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ עֲרַאי, בְּמִקְרֶה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לִפְרָקִים, כֵּן תֵּלְכוּ עֲרַאי בְּמִצְווֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the sages read it as casual, by chance, only now and then, so you keep the commandments only casually.

sources.quote: וּמְנַחֵם פֵּרֵשׁ לְשׁוֹן מְנִיעָה
sources.says: Rashi says Menachem explained it as holding back.

sources.quote: וְאִם תְּהָכוּן קֳדָמַי בְּקַשְׁיוּ
sources.says: Onkelos translates: if you walk before Me with stubbornness.

sources.quote: אמרו רבים שפירושו גבורה ונצוח כאיש שיחזק לבו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says many explain it as strength and defiance, like a man who hardens his heart.

26:32.headline: A curse that hides good news
26:32.body: The land will be so empty that even the enemies living there will be stunned. Rashi and Ramban hear comfort in this: the land will not settle down for anyone else, and will wait for Israel to return.

sources.quote: זוֹ מִדָּה טוֹבָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁלֹּא יִמְצְאוּ הָאוֹיְבִים נַחַת רוּחַ בְּאַרְצָם
sources.says: Rashi says this is a kindness to Israel, since the enemies will find no contentment in their land.

sources.quote: הִיא בְּשׂוֹרָה טוֹבָה מְבַשֶּׂרֶת בְּכָל הַגָּלֻיּוֹת, שֶׁאֵין אַרְצֵנוּ מְקַבֶּלֶת אֶת אוֹיְבֵינוּ
sources.says: Ramban says it is good news for every exile: our land does not accept our enemies.

26:34.headline: The land makes up for the rest years it was denied
26:34.body: Rashi reads תרצה as appease: the land calms God's anger over the sabbatical years that were not kept. Ibn Ezra reads it as pay off, like a hired worker who completes his days.

sources.quote: תְּפַיֵּס אֶת כַּעַס הַמָּקוֹם שֶׁכָּעַס עַל שְׁמִטּוֹתֶיהָ
sources.says: Rashi says the land will appease God's anger over its neglected sabbatical years.

sources.quote: אז תרצה הארץ וזאת המלה כמו תשלי׳‎ וכן עד ירצה כשכיר יומו
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means to complete, as a hired worker completes his day.

26:37.headline: Tripping over each other, and over each other's sins
26:37.body: Plainly, people fleeing in panic trip over one another. The Talmud and Rashi also read it as one person stumbling because of his brother's sin. This is the source for the idea that all Israel are responsible for one another.

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁיָּרוּצוּ לָנוּס יִכָּשְׁלוּ זֶה בָזֶה
sources.says: Rashi says that when they run to flee they will trip over one another.

sources.quote: זֶה נִכְשָׁל בַּעֲוֹנוֹ שֶׁל זֶה, שֶׁכָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל עֲרֵבִין זֶה לָזֶה
sources.says: Rashi says one stumbles through the other's sin, because all Israel are guarantors for one another.

sources.quote: אִישׁ בַּעֲוֹן אָחִיו, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכּוּלָּן עֲרֵבִים זֶה בָּזֶה
sources.says: The Talmud reads it as a man in his brother's sin, and says it teaches that all are guarantors for each other.

26:42.headline: Jacob borrows a letter from Elijah as a pledge
26:42.body: יעקב is usually spelled without a ו, but here it has one. Rashi says Jacob's name is spelled full five times and Elijah's name is missing its ו five times. Jacob took the letter as a pledge that Elijah will come to announce the redemption.

sources.quote: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה מְקוֹמוֹת נִכְתַּב מָלֵא, וְאֵלִיָּהוּ חָסֵר בַּחֲמִשָּׁה מְקוֹמוֹת — יַעֲקֹב נָטַל אוֹת מִשְּׁמוֹ שֶׁל אֵלִיָּהוּ עֵרָבוֹן שֶׁיָּבֹא וִיבַשֵּׂר גְּאֻלַּת בָּנָיו
sources.says: Rashi says Jacob's name is written full in five places and Elijah's is missing a letter in five, because Jacob took a letter from Elijah's name as a pledge that he will come and announce his children's redemption.

26:46.headline: Teachings, in the plural: the written Torah and the oral
26:46.body: The verse says תורות, teachings, not Torah. Rashi says the plural points to two Torahs, one written and one oral, and that both were given to Moses at Sinai.

sources.quote: אַחַת בִּכְתָב וְאַחַת בְּעַל פֶּה, מַגִּיד שֶׁכֻּלָּם נִתְּנוּ לְמֹשֶׁה בְּסִינַי
sources.says: Rashi says one is written and one is oral, and it tells us all were given to Moses at Sinai.

27:2.headline: The same verb means 'say clearly' here and 'be hidden' elsewhere
27:2.body: Rashi reads יפלא as spelling the vow out in words. Chizkuni points out that the same verb in Deuteronomy 17:8, כי יפלא ממך דבר, means a matter hidden from you, the opposite sense.

sources.quote: כי יפלא. יַפְרִישׁ בְּפִיו
sources.says: Rashi says it means he sets the vow apart by saying it with his mouth.

sources.quote: מתיבות שיש להם שני פנים בפירושם וזה למפרע מזה שהרי מצינו כי יפלא ממך דבר למשפט. שהוא לשון העלמה
sources.says: Chizkuni says this is one of the words with two opposite senses, since in 'if a matter is hidden from you in judgment' it means hiding.

sources.quote: לא אמר ידר נדר אלא יפליא, מלשון פלאות חכמה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the verse chose יפליא over plain 'vows' because it comes from the word for the wonders of wisdom.

27:2.headline: An extra letter in this word that Rashi says he cannot explain
27:2.body: The usual word for value is ערך, but here it ends with an extra כ. Rashi says he does not know where the doubled letter comes from, and Ibn Ezra says grammarians call it extra while some read it as speaking to the priest: your valuation.

sources.quote: כתב רש"י ז"ל ערכך כמו ערך, וכפל הכפי"ן לא ידעתי מאיזה לשון הוא
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya quotes Rashi: ערכך means ערך, and Rashi does not know what the doubled כ comes from.

sources.quote: וכ״ף בערכך על דעת כל המדקדקים נוסף והטעם בערך ויש אומרים כי הכ״ף לנכח הכהן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says all the grammarians treat the כ as extra, and some say it addresses the priest.

sources.quote: ערכך - שני הכפין כפל הוא, כמו שתאמר מאודם אדמימות
sources.says: Rashbam says the two כs are a doubling, like the doubled letters in the word for reddishness.

27:3.headline: Here 'value' is a fixed sum by age, not a price
27:3.body: ערך normally means worth or price. Rashi says it is not a price here: whether the person is precious or plain, the sum is fixed only by age.

sources.quote: אֵין עֵרֶךְ זֶה לְשׁוֹן דָּמִים, אֶלָּא בֵּין שֶׁהוּא יָקָר בֵּין שֶׁהוּא זוֹל, כְּפִי שָׁנָיו הוּא הָעֵרֶךְ הַקָּצוּב עָלָיו
sources.says: Rashi says this ערך does not mean price: dear or cheap, the set sum goes by the person's years.

27:8.headline: To value someone is to set him beside a sum
27:8.body: The root ערך means to lay things out in a row. Ibn Ezra says the priest sets the person side by side with a sum, the same sense as אין ערוך אליך, nothing can be set beside you.

sources.quote: שיושם הנערך במערכה אחת עם כך וכך וכמוהו אין ערוך אליך
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the person is placed in one row with such-and-such a sum, as in 'none can be compared to you'.

27:8.headline: Only someone who can be stood up can be valued
27:8.body: The verse says the person is stood before the priest. The Sifra reads this strictly: someone who has died, or is dying and cannot be stood up, has no valuation.

sources.quote: להוציא את המת. אוציא את המת ולא אוציא את הגוסס
sources.says: The Sifra says the phrase leaves out the dead, and asks whether the dying are left out too.

sources.quote: את שיש לו 'העמדה' יש לו 'הערכה', ואת שאין לו 'העמדה' אין לו 'הערכה'
sources.says: The Sifra answers that whoever can be stood up can be valued, and whoever cannot, cannot.

27:10.headline: Swap a holy animal and both animals become holy
27:10.body: If someone trades an animal set aside for God, the substitute becomes holy and the first stays holy. Maimonides gives the reason: if swapping bad for good were allowed, people would swap good for bad and call it better.

sources.quote: כי אילו היה מותר להחליף את הרע בטוב – היו מחליפים את הטוב ברע, ואומרים שזה טוב יותר
sources.says: Maimonides says that if trading bad for good were allowed, people would trade good for bad and say it was better.

sources.quote: שאם יתיר לו להחליף רע בטוב יבא להחליף הטוב ברע ויאמר טוב הוא
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya gives the same reason: allow bad for good and he will come to trade good for bad and call it good.

27:28.headline: Does a devoted gift go to the priests or to the Temple?
27:28.body: חרם means something devoted to God, but the verse does not say to whom. Rashi reports that the sages split: some say a plain חרם goes to the Temple's upkeep, others say it goes to the priests.

sources.quote: נֶחְלְקוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ בַּדָּבָר
sources.says: Rashi says the sages disagree about it.

sources.quote: וְיֵשׁ שֶׁאָמְרוּ, סְתָם חֲרָמִים לַכֹּהֵן
sources.says: Rashi says some hold that an unspecified חרם goes to the priest.

sources.quote: ר' יהודה בן בתירה אומר סתם חרמים לבדק הבית
sources.says: The Sifrei records Rabbi Yehudah ben Beteira saying an unspecified חרם goes to the upkeep of the Temple.

27:34.headline: 'These are the commandments': no prophet may add new ones
27:34.body: The book ends with the word אלה, these. The sages read it as closing the list: from now on no prophet may make up a new commandment.

sources.quote: אין נביא רשאי לחדש עוד דבר מעתה
sources.says: Chizkuni says that from now on no prophet may introduce anything new.

sources.quote: ודרשו רז"ל בתורת כהנים אלה המצות שאין נביא רשאי לחדש דבר מעתה
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the Sifra: 'these are the commandments' teaches that no prophet may add anything from now on.

5:1.headline: An extra letter in 'not' recalls the six days of creation
5:1.body: The word for 'not' is spelled here with an extra ו, the letter that stands for six. Rabbeinu Bahya says it hints at the six days of creation: a witness who hides what he knows is treated as hiding God's own witness that He made the world.

sources.quote: כי תוספת הוא"ו במלת לוא ירמוז על ששת ימי בראשית, ובא להורות כי מי שכובש עדות לחברו מעלה עליו הכתוב כאלו כבש להקב"ה עדות של חדוש העולם שנברא בששת ימים
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the added ו in לוא hints at the six days of creation, so one who holds back testimony is seen as holding back testimony that the world was made in six days.

5:5.headline: Confessing is read as a word for being certain
5:5.body: Rabbeinu Bahya links והתודה, 'he shall confess', to ודאי, 'certain'. The man had forgotten his sin and was unsure of it; now he remembers it and is sure.

sources.quote: שנתן אל לבו וזכר החטא אחר שנעלם ממנו והיה מסופק בו, וחוזר לודאי, וזהו והתודה מלשון ודאי
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says the man recalled the sin he had forgotten and moved from doubt to certainty, and so והתודה comes from the word ודאי.

5:15.headline: Is this sin a betrayal, or something hidden under a cloak?
5:15.body: Rashi says מעילה always means turning faithless, the same word used for a wife who betrays her husband. Ibn Ezra ties it to מעיל, a cloak: the act was covered up.

sources.quote: אֵין מְעִילָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם אֶלָּא שִׁנּוּי, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר וַיִּמְעֲלוּ בֵאלֹהֵי אֲבֹתֵיהֶם וַיִּזְנוּ אַחֲרֵי אֱלֹהֵי עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ (דהי"א ה'), וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר בְּסוֹטָה וּמָעֲלָה בוֹ מָעַל
sources.says: Rashi says מעילה everywhere means a change of loyalty, as when Israel turned to other gods and as with a wife suspected of betrayal.

sources.quote: תמעל מעל. דבר שנתכסה עליו מגזרת מעיל
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word means something covered over, from the same root as מעיל, a cloak.

5:15.headline: Why this offering is called asham and not chatat
5:15.body: Ramban asks why one sin offering is called אשם and another חטאת. He says אשם comes from words for ruin and punishment, for a grave sin; חטאת comes from missing the mark, as a slinger who would not miss a hair.

sources.quote: וְהַנִּרְאֶה בְּעֵינַי כִּי שֵׁם "אָשָׁם" מוֹרֶה עַל דָּבָר גָּדוֹל אֲשֶׁר הָעוֹשׂוֹ יִתְחַיֵּב לִהְיוֹת שָׁמֵם וְאָבֵד בּוֹ
sources.says: Ramban says the name אשם points to a grave matter that makes the doer liable to be left desolate and lost.

sources.quote: וְחַטָּאת מוֹרָה עַל דָּבָר נָטָה בּוֹ מִן הַדֶּרֶךְ, מִלְּשׁוֹן "אֶל הַשַּׂעֲרָה וְלֹא יַחֲטִא
sources.says: Ramban says חטאת points to straying from the path, as in the verse about slingers who aim at a hair and do not miss.

5:15.headline: The ram, איל, read as 'a strong one': two years old
5:15.body: Rashi hears in איל the word for strength, as in 'the mighty (אילי) of the land' in Ezekiel. So this ram must be a strong one, two years old.

sources.quote: איל. לְשׁוֹן קָשֶׁה, כְּמוֹ וְאֶת אֵילֵי הָאָרֶץ לָקָח (יחזקאל י"ז), אַף כָּאן קָשֶׁה — בֶּן שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
sources.says: Rashi says איל means hard or strong, as in Ezekiel's 'the mighty of the land', and so the animal is two years old.

sources.quote: איל תמים קשה בן שתי שנים
sources.says: Chizkuni likewise says the ram is a hard one, two years old.

5:19.headline: The same letters three times: first a noun, last a verb
5:19.body: The verse says אשם three times in a row. Rashi says the vowels tell them apart: the first names the offering, and the last is a verb, 'he has become guilty'.

sources.quote: הָרִאשׁוֹן כֻּלּוֹ קָמוּץ, שֶׁהוּא שֵׁם דָּבָר, וְהָאַחֲרוֹן חֶצְיוֹ קָמָץ וְחֶצְיוֹ פַּתָּח שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן פָּעַל
sources.says: Rashi says the first אשם is all qamats and is a noun, while the last is half qamats and half patach and is a verb.

5:21.headline: Robbing versus oppressing: how עשק differs from גזל
5:21.body: Rashi says עשק is holding back a hired worker's pay. Ibn Ezra says גזל is taking by force and עשק is taking in secret. Rabbeinu Bahya cites the Talmud: עשק is falsely saying 'I already paid you.'

sources.quote: או עשק. הוּא שְֹכַר שָֹכִיר
sources.says: Rashi says עשק is the wage of a hired worker, held back.

sources.quote: בגזל. בחזקה כמו ויגזול את החנית: עשק. בסתר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says גזל is taking by force and עשק is taking in secret.

sources.quote: איזהו גזל ואיזהו עשק, יש לך בידי ואיני נותן לך זהו גזל, נתתיו לך זהו עשק
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya cites the Talmud: 'I have it and will not give it' is גזל; 'I already gave it to you' is עשק.

6:2.headline: Why it is called עולה: all of it goes up
6:2.body: Ibn Ezra says the offering is called עולה, going up, because all of it goes up on the altar. Tur HaArokh, citing him, adds that the priests get no share of it.

sources.quote: היא העולה. נקראת כן בעבור שהיא עולה כלה על המזבח
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it is called עולה because all of it goes up on the altar.

sources.quote: קרויה עולה בשביל שעולה כולה למזבח ואין לכהנים בה חלק
sources.says: Tur HaArokh, citing Ibn Ezra, says it is called עולה because it all goes up to the altar and the priests have no share in it.

6:3.headline: מדו: his garment, cut to his own measure
6:3.body: מדו means his garment, as Rashbam shows from another verse. Rashi hears מדה, measure, in it: the tunic must fit him exactly.

sources.quote: ומדיו קרועים לשון בגדים
sources.says: Rashbam says מדו is a word for clothes, as in his garments torn.

sources.quote: מדו בד. הִיא הַכֻּתֹּנֶת
sources.says: Rashi says מדו is the tunic.

sources.quote: שֶׁתְּהֵא כְמִדָּתוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the word teaches that it must be his size.

6:4.headline: Change clothes to carry out the ashes: a matter of manners
6:4.body: Rashi says this is not a strict duty but good manners. Clothes worn to cook a pot for your master should not be worn to pour his wine, so the priest changes into lesser clothes to carry the ashes.

sources.quote: אֵין זוֹ חוֹבָה אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says this is not an obligation but good manners.

sources.quote: בְּגָדִים שֶׁבִּשֵּׁל בָּהֶן קְדֵרָה לְרַבּוֹ, אַל יִמְזֹג בָּהֶן כּוֹס לְרַבּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says clothes in which one cooked a pot for his master should not be worn to pour his master's cup.

sources.quote: וְלָבַשׁ בְּגָדִים אֲחֵרִים פְּחוּתִין מֵהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says he puts on other clothes, of lesser quality.

6:8.headline: A handful measured by the hand, not by a tool
6:8.body: Rashi reads בקמצו, with his fist, to mean the priest may not make a measuring vessel for the handful. His own hand is the measure.

sources.quote: שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲשֶֹה מִדָּה לַקֹּמֶץ
sources.says: Rashi says he should not make a measuring vessel for the handful.

6:14.headline: מרבכת: scalded in boiling water, or made soft with oil
6:14.body: Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner, and some read it as soft while others read it as quickly made. Rashi says the dough is fully scalded in boiling water, while Rashbam says it is made soft with oil.

sources.quote: מרבכת. אין לו אח ויש מי שאומרים רכה ויש מי שאומרים במהרה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the word has no partner; some say it means soft and some say quickly.

sources.quote: מרבכת. חֲלוּטָה בְּרוֹתְחִין כָּל צָרְכָּהּ
sources.says: Rashi says it is fully scalded in boiling water.

sources.quote: מרבכת - לפי ענינו רכה בשמן
sources.says: Rashbam says by its context it means soft with oil.

6:19.headline: From the word for sin, a word for removing sin
6:19.body: המחטא looks like it comes from חטא, sin, but here it means the priest who takes sin away. Ibn Ezra says it is the one who sprinkles the blood, and many read it as cleansing, as in תחטאני באזוב, purge me with hyssop.

sources.quote: טעמו הזורק דם כאילו אמר המסיר חטא החוטא
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it means the one who sprinkles the blood, as if to say the one who removes the sinner's sin.

sources.quote: ורבי המפרשים אמרו כי טעם המחטא רוחץ או מטהר וכן תחטאני באזוב ואטהר
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says most commentators read it as one who washes or purifies, as in purge me with hyssop.

sources.quote: הָעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדוֹתֶיהָ — שֶׁהִיא נַעֲשֵׂית חַטָּאת עַל יָדוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is the priest who performs its service, through whom it becomes a sin offering.

6:21.headline: Scoured like beauty treatments, or polished like spears
6:21.body: Rashi links ומרק to תמרוקי הנשים, the women's beauty treatments in the book of Esther. Ibn Ezra ties it to מרקו הרמחים, polish the spears.

sources.quote: ומרק. לְשׁוֹן תַּמְרוּקֵי הַנָּשִׁים
sources.says: Rashi says ומרק is the language of the women's beauty treatments.

sources.quote: מגזרת מרקו הרמחים
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it comes from the same root as polish the spears.

8:2.headline: 'Take Aaron': not by the hand, but with words
8:2.body: קח usually means to take hold of something. Rashi says it means to win Aaron over with words. The Sifra asks whether Moses carried people on his back, and answers that God meant: take them with words.

sources.quote: קחנו בדברים ומשכהו
sources.says: Rashi says it means take him with words and draw him in.

sources.quote: וכי מפשיל היה משה בני אדם לאחריו
sources.says: The Sifra asks whether Moses used to carry people on his back.

sources.quote: קחם בדברים שלא יהיה לבם לדבר אחר
sources.says: The Sifra says God meant: take them with words, so their hearts are not turned elsewhere.

sources.quote: היה במשמע שנתקרב אהרן
sources.says: The Sifra says the word showed that Aaron had been brought close again after the golden calf.

8:3.headline: All Israel gathered at one doorway, a small space holding many
8:3.body: The whole people is told to gather at the entrance of the Tent. Rashi, from the midrash, says this is one of the places where a small space held a great many people. The commentators stop here because the gathering seems impossible.

sources.quote: זה אחד מן המקומות שהחזיק מעט את המרבה
sources.says: Rashi says this is one of the places where a little held a lot.

sources.quote: אמר רבי אלעזר כל ישראל ששים רבוא ואת אומר אל פתח אהל מועד
sources.says: Rabbi Elazar in the midrash asks how six hundred thousand could stand at the Tent's doorway.

8:5.headline: 'This is what God commanded': Moses says he is not favoring his brother
8:5.body: Before installing Aaron, Moses tells the people 'this is the thing God commanded'. Rashi says Moses meant: do not think I do this for my own honor or my brother's.

sources.quote: ואל תאמרו לכבודי ולכבוד אחי אני עושה
sources.says: Rashi says Moses told them not to think he acted for his own honor or his brother's.

8:8.headline: The Urim: not the breastplate stones, but a written Name of God
8:8.body: The Urim and Thummim are put into the breastplate, but the verse never says what they were. Rashi says they were a writing of God's full Name. Ibn Ezra notes they were separate from the stones, and Rabbeinu Bahya says their answers were a level of holy spirit below prophecy.

sources.quote: כתב של שם המפרש
sources.says: Rashi says the Urim was a writing of God's explicit Name.

sources.quote: כן האורים והתומים אינם אבני החושן
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says the Urim and Thummim were not the stones of the breastplate.

sources.quote: ומדרגה היתה ממדרגות רוח הקדש למטה ממדרגת הנבואה ולמעלה מבת קול
sources.says: Rabbeinu Bahya says it was a level of holy spirit, below prophecy and above a heavenly voice.

8:15.headline: Here חטא means to cleanse the altar, not to sin
8:15.body: The root חטא usually means to sin. Here Moses 'un-sins' the altar. Rashi says he purified it from common use so it could enter holiness. Ramban adds that the blood is what did this.

sources.quote: חטאו וטהרו מזרות לכנס לקדשה
sources.says: Rashi says he cleansed and purified it from being ordinary, so it could enter holiness.

sources.quote: וילמד בכאן כי בדם נעשה זה
sources.says: Ramban says the verse teaches that this was done with the blood.

8:22.headline: The 'ram of filling' makes the priests complete
8:22.body: מלואים comes from 'to fill'. Rashi says it means completing: it makes the priests whole in their office. Ramban says it gives them a 'full hand' for God's service, and this ram carries the name because it is the last of these offerings.

sources.quote: שמלואים לשון שלמים, שממלאין ומשלימין את הכהנים בכהנתם
sources.says: Rashi says מלואים means completeness, since it fills and completes the priests in their priesthood.

sources.quote: כי ענין המלואים שתהיה להם יד שלמה לעבד את עבדת ה'
sources.says: Ramban says the filling means they will have a complete hand to do God's service.

sources.quote: בעבור שהוא סוף הקרבנות הללו
sources.says: Ramban says this ram has the name because it is the last of these offerings.

8:32.headline: Here the letter ב, 'in', means מ, 'from'
8:32.body: The verse says 'what is left in the meat and in the bread'. Ramban and Chizkuni say the letter ב here works like מ: what is left over from the meat and the bread.

sources.quote: הבי"ת בשתי המלות תשמש כמו מ"ם, והנותר מן הבשר ומן הלחם
sources.says: Ramban says the ב in both words works like מ: what is left from the meat and from the bread.

sources.quote: בבשר ובלחם מבשר ומלחם
sources.says: Chizkuni says 'in the meat and in the bread' means 'from the meat and from the bread'.
